title: Find All Occurrences of a Suspicious Pattern
real_world_story: A plagiarism detection system receives a suspicious phrase or text pattern and needs to locate every position where that pattern appears inside a document.

real_world_connection.system: Plagiarism detection and document search system
real_world_connection.input_represents: The document and a suspicious text pattern
real_world_connection.target_represents: All positions where the suspicious pattern occurs
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Efficiently searching for a pattern throughout a document using prefix information

problem_statement: Given a document string and a pattern string, find all starting indices where the pattern occurs in the document. Overlapping occurrences must also be included.
task: Search the document for every occurrence of the given pattern and print their zero-based starting indices.
input_format: The first line contains the document string. The second line contains the pattern string.
output_format: Print all zero-based starting indices of the pattern separated by spaces. If the pattern does not occur, print -1.
constraints: Document and pattern contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The pattern 'abc' starts at indices 2 and 5 in the document.
The pattern occurs at indices 0, 1, and 2, including overlapping occurrences.

expected_algorithm.name: KMP Pattern Matching
expected_algorithm.reason: KMP uses a prefix table to avoid unnecessary comparisons and efficiently finds all occurrences of a pattern in a large document.

hint: Build the Longest Prefix Suffix array for the pattern.
Scan the document while maintaining the current matched pattern length.
After finding a complete match, continue using the prefix table to detect overlapping occurrences.
real_world_takeaway: Efficient pattern matching allows plagiarism systems to quickly locate suspicious phrases even in very large documents.
